'''Atayuta Shrine''' (阿多由太神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Takayama City|Takayama City]], {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|en|Gifu Prefecture|qid=Q131277|lt=Gifu Prefecture|1=Gifu Prefecture}}.
It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and one of the eight shrines listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} for {{ill|Hida Province|en|Hida Province|qid=Q1056535|lt=Hida Province|1=Hida Province}}. The shrine's {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qid=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} classification was as a gōsha. Its main shrine building is designated as a {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=National Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}.<ref name="AtayutaHonden">{{Cite web|language=ja|date= |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/144808 |title=阿多由太神社本殿 |publisher=[[Cultural Heritage Online]]/[[Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)|Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=2021-06-26|qq=}}</ref> The building was also recognized in 2016 as part of the {{ill|Japan Heritage|en|Japan Heritage|qid=Q18382798|lt=Japan Heritage|1=Japan Heritage}} site "Hida Masters' Skills and Spirit / Medieval Temple and Shrine Architecture of Kokufu Basin."<ref>{{Cite web|language=ja|date= |url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story029/ |title=Japan Heritage Portal: Hida Masters' Skills and Spirit|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=2019-02-21|qq=}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The exact date of the shrine's founding is unknown. According to the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}, it was awarded the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade, in the 9th year of the {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|qid=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan era|1=Zhenguan}} (867 CE), confirming its status as a highly esteemed shrine since ancient times. During the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}, it was referred to as "Gongen Shrine." In the {{ill|Bunka|en|Bunka|qid=Q1373146|lt=Bunka era|1=Bunka}} (1804–1818), a study erroneously identified it as the {{ill|Arashiro Shrine|ja|荒城神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arashiro Shrine|1=Araki Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11618425}} of the Engishiki, but subsequent investigations confirmed it as Atayuta Shrine. It was renamed accordingly.
== Cultural Properties ==
{{commonscat|Atayuta-jinja|qq=}}
=== National Important Cultural Properties ===
* '''Main Shrine''' - Built in the late {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period|1=Muromachi period}}, it features the rare "Three-Bay Flowing Style Sheltered Platform" (三間社流見世棚造, sangensha nagare misedana-zukuri),<ref>The three-bay style has three spaces between its four pillars, with the flowing style roof extended to create a raised platform at the front, often found in small shrine buildings.</ref> and a wooden shingle roof. It was designated in {{ill|1961|en|1961|qid=Q3696|lt=1961|1=1961}} (Showa 36).<ref name="AtayutaHonden" />
=== Gifu Prefecture Important Cultural Properties ===
* '''Wooden Guardian Figures (Pair)''' - Wooden deity statues believed to date back to the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}.<ref>{{Cite web|language=ja|date= |url=http://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/kyoiku/bunka/bunkazai/17768/cyoukoku/mokuzouzui.html |title=Guardian Figures |publisher=Gifu Prefecture |accessdate=2016-02-06|qq=}}</ref>
=== Takayama City Important Cultural Properties ===
* '''Atayuta Shrine Inari Shrine Building''' - Constructed during the {{ill|Kaei|en|Kaei|qid=Q1146125|lt=Kaei era|1=Kaei}} (1848–1854).
